requirement_text: Standalone must expose versioned shopper, admin, integration, webhook, and diagnostic API surfaces as appropriate.
REST and Store API handlers must call the same application services as internal flows.
OpenAPI must describe routes, schemas, authentication, errors, examples, pagination, and versioning.
JSON Schema must define public request and response contracts.
Mutating endpoints must support idempotency keys where repetition is possible.
Responses and logs must carry correlation or request IDs.
Concurrent resource changes should support ETag or equivalent optimistic concurrency where appropriate.
Authorization must be capability and object scoped.
Public responses must expose only customer-safe fields.
Errors must be structured, stable, localized at presentation boundaries, and fail closed.
Public contracts must be classified stable, experimental, or internal with deprecation policy.
API rate and abuse protection must be appropriate to quote and geography cost.
Every data class must have an explicit retention and cleanup policy.
Quotes and transient traces must expire without deleting contractual snapshots.
Logs must be configurable and redacted.
Order snapshots and policy history must not be garbage collected.
Deactivation must not delete data.
Uninstall deletion must require explicit merchant intent and remain bounded to plugin-owned data.
Background cleanup must use bounded scheduled work and must not delete shared Action Scheduler tables.
Major runtime modules and adapters must support controlled enablement.
Feature flags must preserve configuration and history when disabled.
A global emergency disable must stop Delivery Engine checkout effects safely.
Flags must support gradual rollout or bounded activation where appropriate.
Flag state and operational impact must be visible in diagnostics.
Business rules must have draft, published, retired, and scheduled lifecycle states.
Rules must retain version, effective-from, effective-until, author, and change reason.
Only published and currently effective rules may drive customer results.
Rule precedence and conflicts must be deterministic and diagnosable.
Historical orders must retain the applied rule or policy version.
Rule changes must support impact preview or dry-run.
Emergency disable must not destroy rule history.
Each order line must retain immutable product, variation, quantity, fulfillment, and selected-offer facts.
Snapshots must retain destination or pickup endpoint and delivery-group identity.
Snapshots must retain quoted amount, currency, rate-card identity, and quote status.
Snapshots must retain customer-facing offer label, description, and estimate.
Snapshots must retain applied DeliveryQuote identity and pricing-policy version.
Snapshots must retain fulfillment labels and promise-policy version.
Snapshots must retain Return Policy and Refund Policy versions, summaries, full text, and exceptions.
Historical snapshots must never be rewritten from current configuration.
Configuration writes must be audited and versioned.
Logs must use WooCommerce logging, correlation IDs, severity, and redaction.
Diagnostics must remain truthful when an analysis is bounded or incomplete.
Cached and uncached matching must preserve equivalent explainability.
Monitoring must not expose private commercial or customer data.
Standalone core must operate with WooCommerce as its only hard application dependency.
WooCommerce owns products, variations, carts, checkout, orders, customers, payments, refunds, taxes, and accounts.
The Delivery Engine must not duplicate merchandise pricing, stock, payment, tax, identity, or product-master authority.
Every administrative write must enforce capability, nonce, validation, and object scope.
Public canonical IDs and selection payloads must be treated as untrusted input.
Money, eligibility, promise, and shipment transitions must be server-authoritative.
Public payloads must exclude supplier, origin, rate-card, internal-cost, margin, and secret data.
Logs and diagnostics must redact personal, address, coordinate, credential, and token data.
Precise addresses and coordinates must have purpose-limited storage and disclosure.
Quote, geography, webhook, and diagnostic interfaces must be rate and abuse protected.
Secrets must never be committed, exported, logged, or shipped in packages.
Imports and uploads must resist path traversal, SSRF, archive abuse, and malicious content.
Security qualification must include runtime behavior, not only static tool output.
Errors must explain recovery without exposing internals or implying false availability.
